rules: When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts are globally enabled if mstatus.xIE=1.
When a hart is executing in privilege mode x, interrupts are globally disabled if mstatus.xIE=0.
Interrupts for privilege modes w < x are globally disabled when the hart is executing in privilege mode x, regardless of the setting of mstatus.wIE.
Interrupts for privilege modes y > x are globally enabled when the hart is executing in privilege mode x, regardless of the setting of mstatus.yIE.
If supervisor mode is not implemented, mstatus.SIE and mstatus.SPIE are read-only 0.
When a trap is taken from privilege mode y into privilege mode x, mstatus.xPIE is set to the value of mstatus.xIE.
When a trap is taken from privilege mode y into privilege mode x, mstatus.xIE is set to 0.
When a trap is taken from privilege mode y into privilege mode x, mstatus.xPP is set to y.
When an xRET instruction is executed and mstatus.xPP holds value y, mstatus.xIE is set to the value of mstatus.xPIE.
When an xRET instruction is executed and mstatus.xPP holds value y, the privilege mode is changed to y.
When an xRET instruction is executed and mstatus.xPP holds value y, mstatus.xPIE is set to 1.
When an xRET instruction is executed and mstatus.xPP holds value y, mstatus.xPP is set to the least-privileged supported mode (U if U-mode is implemented, else M).
When an xRET instruction is executed and the new privilege mode y is not M, mstatus.MPRV is set to 0.
mstatus.xPP fields are WARL fields that can only hold privilege mode x and any implemented privilege mode lower than x.
If privilege mode x is not implemented, mstatus.xPP is read-only 0.
When mstatus.MDT is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write, mstatus.MIE is cleared to 0.
For RV64, when mstatus.MDT is set to 1 by an explicit CSR write, mstatus.MIE is cleared to 0 regardless of the value written to mstatus.MIE by the same write.
mstatus.MIE can be set to 1 by an explicit CSR write only if mstatus.MDT is 0 or, for RV64, mstatus.MDT is being set to 0 by the same write.
When a trap is to be taken into M-mode and mstatus.MDT is 0, mstatus.MDT is set to 1.
When MRET or SRET is executed in M-mode, mstatus.MDT is set to 0.
When MRET or SRET is executed in M-mode and the new privilege mode is U, VS, or VU, mstatus.SDT is set to 0.
When MRET or SRET is executed in M-mode and the new privilege mode is VU, vsstatus.SDT is set to 0.
When MNRET is executed and the new privilege mode is not M, mstatus.MDT is set to 0.
When MNRET is executed and the new privilege mode is U, VS, or VU, mstatus.SDT is set to 0.
When MNRET is executed and the new privilege mode is VU, vsstatus.SDT is set to 0.
When MXLEN=64 and S-mode is not supported, mstatus.SXL is read-only 0.
When MXLEN=64 and U-mode is not supported, mstatus.UXL is read-only 0.
If S-mode is implemented, the legal values of mstatus.UXL exclude those that would cause UXLEN to be greater than SXLEN.
When mstatus.MPRV=0, explicit memory accesses use the translation and protection mechanisms of the current privilege mode.
When mstatus.MPRV=1, load and store memory addresses are translated and protected as though the current privilege mode were set to mstatus.MPP.
mstatus.MPRV is read-only 0 if U-mode is not supported.
When mstatus.MXR=0, only loads from pages marked readable (R=1) succeed.
When mstatus.MXR=1, loads from pages marked either readable (R=1) or executable (X=1) succeed.
mstatus.MXR is read-only 0 if S-mode is not supported.
When mstatus.SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) fault.
When mstatus.SUM=1, S-mode memory accesses to pages accessible by U-mode (U=1) are permitted.
mstatus.SUM is read-only 0 if S-mode is not supported or if satp.MODE is read-only 0.
When mstatus.MBE=0, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses from M-mode (with mstatus.MPRV=0) are little-endian.
When mstatus.MBE=1, non-instruction-fetch memory accesses from M-mode (with mstatus.MPRV=0) are big-endian.
If S-mode is not supported, mstatus.SBE is read-only 0.
When mstatus.SBE=0, explicit load and store memory accesses from S-mode are little-endian.
When mstatus.SBE=1, explicit load and store memory accesses from S-mode are big-endian.
If U-mode is not supported, mstatus.UBE is read-only 0.
When mstatus.UBE=0, explicit load and store memory accesses from U-mode are little-endian.
When mstatus.UBE=1, explicit load and store memory accesses from U-mode are big-endian.
When mstatus.TVM=1, attempts to read or write the satp CSR or execute SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstatus.TVM=0, attempts to read or write the satp CSR or execute SFENCE.VMA or SINVAL.VMA in S-mode are permitted.
mstatus.TVM is read-only 0 when S-mode is not supported.
When mstatus.TW=1 and WFI is executed in any less-privileged mode and does not complete within a bounded time limit, WFI causes an illegal-instruction exception.
mstatus.TW is read-only 0 when there are no modes less privileged than M.
When mstatus.TSR=1, attempts to execute SRET in S-mode raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstatus.TSR=0, attempts to execute SRET in S-mode are permitted.
mstatus.TSR is read-only 0 when S-mode is not supported.
When mstatus.FS=0 (Off), any instruction attempting to read or write floating-point state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstatus.VS=0 (Off), any instruction attempting to read or write vector state causes an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstatus.FS, mstatus.VS, and mstatus.XS are all read-only 0, mstatus.SD is always 0.
mstatus.SD is set to 1 when either mstatus.FS, mstatus.VS, or mstatus.XS encode a Dirty state (0b11).
